content.text:
Yes — `react/jsx-max-props-per-line` from `eslint-plugin-react` (already a dependency here). Set it to `["error", { maximum: 1, when: "always" }]` and it'll force every prop onto its own line, even for single-prop or otherwise-short components (`when: "multiline"` only applies once a tag has already wrapped, which usually isn't what people mean by "insist"). You'd likely pair it with `react/jsx-first-prop-new-line: ["error", "always"]` so the first prop doesn't sit on the opening-tag line, and `react/jsx-closing-bracket-location` for the closing `>` placement — the same one-per-line style you already enforce for Mantine imports.

One tradeoff: this project has no Prettier, so there's no autoformat fighting the rule, but `eslint --fix` will happily rewrite every existing JSX tag with 2+ props, which is a large diff across the codebase.

Want me to add these rules to [eslint.config.mjs](eslint.config.mjs) and run `lint:fix`?
Write a new Jira Story for this

input.summary: Enforce one JSX prop per line via ESLint
input.description:
**As a** developer working on this codebase
**I want** every JSX prop to be written on its own line
**So that** component markup is consistently readable and diffs stay small when a prop is added or changed

## Background

`eslint-plugin-react` is already a project dependency but does not currently enforce one-prop-per-line JSX formatting. This mirrors the existing convention for `@mantine/*` imports (one specifier per line, trailing comma).

## Proposed rules (`eslint.config.mjs`)

- `react/jsx-max-props-per-line`: `["error", { maximum: 1, when: "always" }]` — forces every prop onto its own line, even for single-prop or otherwise-short tags (`when: "multiline"` only kicks in once a tag has already wrapped).
- `react/jsx-first-prop-new-line`: `["error", "always"]` — keeps the first prop off the opening-tag line.
- `react/jsx-closing-bracket-location` — consistent placement of the closing `>`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Rules added to `eslint.config.mjs`.
- [ ] `npm run lint:fix` run across the codebase to reformat existing JSX with 2+ props onto multiple lines.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` pass with zero errors/warnings.
- [ ] No behavioural changes — formatting only.

## Notes

No Prettier is configured in this repo, so there's no autoformat conflict — but `lint:fix` will produce a large diff across most `.tsx` files touching JSX with multiple props. Consider doing this as an isolated, reviewable commit separate from any functional change.
